Quotes / Elizabeth Anscombe / Q0526

“It would be a great improvement if, instead of "morally wrong," one always named a genus such as "untruthful," "unchaste," "unjust."” — Elizabeth Anscombe

Elizabeth Anscombe, Modern Moral Philosophy (1958)

About this citation

An article, not a book — and one that changed the vocabulary. Its three claims are widely quoted separately, but the argument for them is cumulative and the second depends on the first.

Reading the cited source

The archive attributes this English wording to Modern Moral Philosophy (1958) and files it under Analytic Philosophy.

About Elizabeth Anscombe

How to read this passage

Virtue ethics asks not only which acts are right, but what kind of person one becomes. Courage, justice, temperance, and wisdom are classic Western lists; Confucian ren and yi offer related but distinct vocabularies. This passage enters that discussion through virtue, language, justice.
